channel.title: The Hollywood Reporter - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Hollywood Reporter (hollywoodreporter.com)

item.title: NBCUniversal and ABM Industries Rehire More Than 100 Union Janitors, Averting Major Protest
item.description: The service workers were laid off on Monday after the entertainment company allegedly canceled deals with a facilities subcontractor at three locations.

item.title: Boulder Int’l Film Fest: Alec Baldwin Set for Live Episode of THR’s ‘Awards Chatter’ Podcast
item.description: The Oscar-nominated and Emmy-winning actor will discuss his life and career on April 11.

item.title: Kevin Williamson Says He Won’t Return to Direct ‘Scream 8’
item.description: The filmmaker, who helmed the Paramount franchise's latest installment, offered an update on the potential future of the horror series.

item.title: LaTanya Richardson Jackson Sends Message to “Wake Up, Stay Woke” at Essence Black Women in Hollywood
item.description: "We who believe in freedom will not rest until it comes," said Richardson Jackson, who was honored alongside Chase Infiniti, Kerry Washington and the women of 'Sinners' at the annual awards luncheon.

item.title: ‘I Love Boosters’ Review: Keke Palmer and Demi Moore in Boots Riley’s Blisteringly Funny, Joyfully Rousing Anti-Capitalist Satire
item.description: Also starring Don Cheadle, Taylour Paige and Naomi Ackie, the SXSW-premiering comedy follows a band of Bay Area shoplifters who get swept up in a larger global scheme.

item.title: ‘Wishful Thinking’ Review: Maya Hawke and Lewis Pullman Conjure Fireworks in a Sharp and Playful High-Concept Romance
item.description: Graham Parkes' directorial debut, premiering at SXSW, centers on a bickering couple whose karmic energy has the ability to trigger storms, stock market bounces and more.

item.title: ‘Kill Me’ Review: Charlie Day and Allison Williams in a Mental Health Murder Mystery That’s More Bruising Than Satisfying
item.description: After waking up from a suicide attempt he can't remember making, a man sets out to solve his own would-be murder in Peter Warren's directorial debut, premiering at SXSW.

item.title: ‘Burning Voice’ Goes Inside Tamara Amer’s Fight for Iraqi Women’s Rights: “I Won’t Shut Up”
item.description: Anna Bruun Nørager's documentary, premiering at CPH:DOX in Copenhagen, comes amid a global backlash: "Extreme conservative forces are trying to push down the fight for women’s rights."

item.title: ‘Something Familiar’ Is a Journey Into Family Bonds and Trauma That Usurps Narratives About Romanian Orphans (Exclusive CPH:DOX Trailer)
item.description: Rachel Taparjan's first feature, debuting at Copenhagen, sees the director and another woman returning to the orphanage where they were adopted, putting her on a path to confronting a painful legacy.
